title: Multiscaling in the Rough Bergomi Model: A Tale of Tails
abstract: arXiv:2601.11305v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The rough Bergomi (rBergomi) model, characterised by its roughness parameter $H$, has been shown to exhibit multiscaling behaviour as $H$ approaches zero. Multiscaling has profound implications for financial modelling: it affects extreme risk estimation, influences optimal portfolio allocation across different time horizons, and challenges traditional option pricing approaches that assume uniscaling behaviours. Understanding whether multiscaling arises primarily from the roughness of volatility paths or from the resulting fat-tailed returns has important implications for financial modelling, option pricing, and risk management. This paper investigates the real source of this multiscaling behaviour by introducing a novel two-stage statistical testing procedure. translated_title: 粗糙Bergomi模型中的多标度性：尾部的故事
translated_abstract: 粗糙Bergomi（rBergomi）模型以其粗糙度参数 $H$ 为特征，已被证明在 $H$ 趋近于零时会表现出多标度行为。多标度对金融建模具有深远的影响：它会影响极端风险的估计，影响不同时间尺度上的最优投资组合配置，并挑战那些假设单一标度行为的传统期权定价方法。理解多标度究竟主要源于波动率路径的粗糙性，还是源于由此产生的肥尾收益，对金融建模、期权定价和风险管理具有重要意义。本文通过引入一种新颖的两阶段统计检验程序来研究这种多标度行为的真正来源。在第一阶段，我们针对单一标度的分数布朗运动过程，确立了rBergomi模型中多标度的存在性。我们通过使用量化多标度……
tldr: 本文提出一种新颖的两阶段统计检验程序，研究粗糙Bergomi模型中多标度行为的真正来源，表明其主要由肥尾收益特性驱动而非波动率路径的粗糙性，这对极端风险估计、投资组合配置和期权定价具有重要意义。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel two-stage statistical testing procedure to investigate the true source of multiscaling in the rough Bergomi model, showing that it is primarily driven by fat-tailed returns rather than the roughness of volatility paths, with significant implications for extreme risk estimation, portfolio allocation, and option pricing.
